'''Telekom Srbija [[List of legal entity types by country#Serbia|a.d.]] Beograd''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Телеком Србија а.д. Београд}}) is a Serbian state-owned [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[Telecommunications company|telecommunications]] [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] [[holding company]] established in May 1997 as a [[joint-stock company]] by spinning off the telecommunications business from PTT Srbija (present-day [[Pošta Srbije]]) and headquartered in [[Belgrade]]. In April 2015, Telekom Srbija started providing most of its services in Serbia under the '''mts''' brand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ekapija.com/news/1112469/mts-postaje-brend-za-sve-usluge-telekoma-srbije|title="mts" postaje brend za sve usluge "Telekoma Srbije"|publisher=ekapija.com|date=6 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ARBK |url=https://arbk.rks-gov.net/page.aspx?id=2,38,174924}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-09-08 |title=Telecommunications |url=https://dialogue-info.com/telecommunications/ |access-date=2022-09-12 |website=The Dialogue}}</ref>

{{asof|2020|post=,}} Telekom Srbija, including its Moja Supernova service platform, was the largest Internet provider in 2020 with a market share of 53.15%, was the second largest cable operator in 2020 with a market share of 44%, and the largest fixed-line telecommunications provider with a market share of 77.5%.<ref name="stats2020">{{cite web |title=PREGLED TRŽIŠTA TELEKOMUNIKACIJA I POŠTANSKIH USLUGA U REPUBLICI SRBIJI U 2020. GODINI |url=https://www.ratel.rs/uploads/documents/empire_plugin/Ratel_Pregled%20trzista_2020_web%20lat.pdf |website=ratel.rs |publisher=RATEL |access-date=21 January 2022 |language=Serbian}}</ref> It is also the largest mobile operator with a market share of 37.27%.<ref name="stats2020" />

==History==
[[File:Telekom-Srbija-Logo.svg|right|thumb|250px|Telekom Srbija's previous logo used from 1997 to 2015.]]
Telekom Srbija a.d. Beograd was set up in 1997, during the process of transformation of [[Pošta Srbije|PTT sistema Srbije]]. In June of that same year, it became the ownership of three shareholders – JP PTT Saobraćaja Srbija (present-day JP Pošta Srbije) (51%), [[Telecom Italia]] (29%), and [[OTE]] Greece (20%).<ref>{{cite news|title=A brief overview of the history of the Post of Serbia|url=https://www.posta.rs/eng/o-nama/istorijat.aspx|work=posta.rs|access-date=21 January 2021|archive-date=20 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420111508/https://www.posta.rs/eng/o-nama/istorijat.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Greece's OTE Join to Buy 49% Stake in Serbian Telecom|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB865866955982055000|work=wsj.com|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

===2003–2015===
JP PTT saobraćaja Srbija (present-day JP Pošta Srbije) became the owner of 80% of the stake after purchasing the shares from the Italian partner, Telecom Italia in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.telekom.rs/telekomeng/Contents/ContentDefault.aspx?temp=0&sid=1181&id=1354|title=About us – History|publisher=Telekom Srbija|access-date=17 April 2013|archive-date=6 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906042238/http://www.telekom.rs/telekomeng/Contents/ContentDefault.aspx?temp=0&sid=1181&id=1354|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2007, the Company regionally expanded into B-H and Montenegro. That same year, [[Mtel Bosnia and Herzegovina|“Telekom Srpske“]]  a.d. [[Banja Luka]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mondo.rs/Info/Drustvo/a42734/Telekom-Srbija-kupio-Telekom-Srpske.html|access-date=20 April 2021|work=mondo.rs|issue=5 December 2006|title=Telekom Srbija kupio Telekom Srpske}}</ref> and Društvo za telekomunikacije [[Mtel Montenegro|m:tel d.o.o.]] [[Podgorica]] were set up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.b92.net/biz/vesti/region.php?yyyy=2007&mm=09&dd=19&nav_id=264121&fs=1|access-date=20 April 2021|work=tanjug.rs|issue=19 September 2007|title=CG: M:tel preuzeo 12,8% tržišta|date=19 September 2007 }}</ref>

In August 2011, the company became the majority owner of Društvo za telekomunikacije HD WIN d.o.o. Beograd ([[Arena Sport]]  TV Channels).<ref>{{cite news|url= https://seenews.com/news/telekom-srbija-becomes-majority-owner-of-arena-sport-tv-channels-205888|title=Telekom Srbija Becomes Majority Owner of Arena Sport TV Channels|publisher=Seenews|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>

In January 2012, the company became the owner of 20% of the share capital which had been held by [[OTE]] Greece until then.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tanjug.rs/news/31380/telekom-serbia-in-states-ownership.htm4|title=Telekom Serbia in state's ownership|publisher=tanjug.rs|access-date=21 January 2021}}{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> That same year, the employees and former employees of Telekom Srbija a.d. Beograd, were presented with an opportunity to become owners of the shares.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rts.rs/page/stories/sr/story/13/Ekonomija/1095816/Besplatne+akcije+%22Telekoma%22.html |title= RTS: Free shares of Telekom|publisher=rts.rs|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

===2015–present===
On 6 January 2015, Telekom Srbija acquired a 55.8 percent of shares in the Dunav banka, becoming its majority owner.<ref>{{cite news|title=Telekom Srbija becomes Dunav Banka majority shareholder|url=http://www.telecompaper.com/news/telekom-srbija-becomes-dunav-banka-majority-shareholder--1058072|access-date=20 March 2015|work=telecompaper.com|issue=6 January 2015}}</ref> Afterwards, the bank changed its name to "mts banka".

As of 2016, it is the largest broadband internet provider (45.9% market share) and the second largest cable television provider (25.0% market share) in Serbia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pregled tržišta telekomunikacija i poštanskih usluga u Republici Srbiji u 2016. godini |url=https://www.ratel.rs/uploads/documents/pdf_documents/documents/Pregled_trzista/Pregled%20trzista_2016.pdf |website=ratel.rs |publisher=RATEL |access-date=21 September 2018 |location=Belgrade |language=sr |date=2017}}</ref>

In November 2018, Telekom Srbija bought domestic cable operator "Kopernikus Technology" for 190 million euros.<ref name="kopernikus2018">{{cite news |last1=Obradović |first1=M. |title=Telekom: Kopernikus smo platili manje od 200 miliona evra |url=https://www.danas.rs/ekonomija/telekom-kopernikus-smo-platili-manje-od-200-miliona-evra/ |accessdate=17 November 2018 |work=danas.rs |date=6 November 2018 |language=Serbian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Serbia's state telco buys cable TV, internet provider Kopernikus -newspaper |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/kopernikus-ma-telekom-srbija/serbias-state-telco-buys-cable-tv-internet-provider-kopernikus-newspaper-idUSL8N1XH2GP |accessdate=17 November 2018 |work=reuters.com |agency=Reuters |date=6 November 2018}}</ref> The transaction made public outrage in Serbia as Kopenikus' market worth at the time of purchase was several times lower than the amount it was purchased for; it was also revealed that major stakeholder in company was a close relative to ruling [[Serbian Progressive Party]] officer.<ref name="kopernikus2018upd">{{cite news |last1=Obradović |first1=M. |title=Milićević: Kopernikus vredi 37,5 miliona evra |url=https://www.danas.rs/ekonomija/milicevic-kopernikus-vredi-375-miliona-evra/ |accessdate=17 November 2018 |work=danas.rs |date=13 November 2018 |language=Serbian}}</ref> Month later, Kopernikus' former owner used much of that money for the purchase of [[B92]] and [[Prva Srpska Televizija]], two television networks with national coverage.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.danas.rs/ljudi/srdjan-milovanovic-of-sor-biznismen-i-folk-producent/ | title=Srđan Milovanović: Of-šor biznismen i folk producent | publisher=Danas | date=6 December 2018 | accessdate=4 April 2021}}</ref>

On 6 January 2019, Telekom Srbija acquired domestic cable operators [[Radijus Vektor]] and "AVcom", in a transaction worth 120 million euros.<ref name="radijusavcom2019">{{cite news |last1=Obradović |first1=M. |title=Telekom grabi ka duopolu sa SBB-om |url=https://www.danas.rs/ekonomija/telekom-grabi-ka-duopolu-sa-sbb-om/ |access-date=13 January 2019 |work=danas.rs |date=9 January 2019 |language=sr}}</ref>

In July 2019, Telekom Srbija acquired another regional cable operator "Telemark".<ref>{{cite news |title=Telekom Srbija kupio kablovskog operatora Telemark |url=https://www.b92.net/biz/vesti/srbija.php?yyyy=2019&mm=07&dd=05&nav_id=1562719 |access-date=4 August 2019 |work=b92.net |date=5 July 2019 |language=sr}}</ref> Later in July, [[Euronews]] and HD-WIN (majority owned by Telekom Srbija) signed a deal to launch the "Euronews Serbia" news channel.<ref>{{cite news |title=Euronews and HD-WIN announce launch of Euronews Serbia |url=https://www.euronews.com/2019/07/15/euronews-and-hd-win-announce-launch-of-euronews-serbia |access-date=4 August 2019 |work=euronews.com |date=16 July 2019}}</ref>

Per 2019 financial report, the total company debt stood at 1.226 billion [[euro]]s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brokeri upozoravaju da prezaduženost obara profit Telekoma |url=https://n1info.rs/biznis/a613944-Brokeri-upozoravaju-da-prezaduzenost-obara-profit-Telekoma/ |access-date=8 November 2026 |work=n1info.rs |agency=Beta |date=26 June 2020}}</ref>

During the rule of [[Serbian Progressive Party]] (SNS), Telekom Srbija was under its direct political control, and over the years has financed over 30 TV stations that were close to the regime.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sretenović |first1=M. |title=Telekom godinama plaćao televizije samo za Vučićevu propagandu |url=https://www.danas.rs/vesti/ekonomija/telekom-propaganda-finansije/ |access-date=8 November 2026 |work=danas.rs |date=3 November 2026}}</ref> Over the years, the company total debt increased to over 5 billion euros;<ref>{{cite news |title=Lučićev oproštajni valcer |url=https://radar.nova.rs/drustvo/telekom-srbija-u-fokusu-pravosudnih-organa/ |access-date=8 November 2026 |work=radar.nova.rs |date=6 November 2026 |language=Serbian}}</ref> per 2025 consolidated financial report, the total company debt was 7 billion euros.<ref name="assertsreport2025" />

== Services and business operations ==
Telekom Srbija's mobile network was established on 9 June 1997. The company launched the provision of mobile services in 1998. 3G technology and [[DSL|ADSL]] Internet services were introduced in 2006, multimedia services ([[IPTV]]) in 2008.<ref>{{Cite news|url= https://www.b92.net/biz/vesti/srbija.php?yyyy=2008&mm=10&dd=15&nav_id=323550|title=Тelekom Srbija to Introduce IPTV|work=b92.net|date=10 October 2008|access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref> Whereas [[4G|LTE (4G)]] technology was introduced in 2015.<ref>{{Cite news|url= https://www.ekapija.com/en/news/1110767/telekom-srbija-launches-4g-network|title=Telekom Srbija launches 4G network|work=еGate|date=4 April 2015|access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref> 

At present, Telekom Srbija provides the following services:

===Mobile telephony===
[[File:MTS logo 1997.png|300px|thumb|right|mts' logo was stylized as "mt:s" until 8 April 2015. This was the first variation of the "mt:s" logo, used from 2005 to 2006.]]
The Mobile Telephony of Serbia (mts) subdivision was created in June 1997 and started operating in August 1998.

===Mobile network technology===
*[[2G]] on 900&nbsp;MHz & 1800&nbsp;MHz
*[[3G]] on 900&nbsp;MHz & 2100&nbsp;MHz
*[[4G]] on 800&nbsp;MHz, 1800&nbsp;MHz & 2100&nbsp;MHz
*[[5G]] on 700&nbsp;MHz, 2600&nbsp;MHz & 3500&nbsp;MHz
The mts signal covers 92.00% of Serbia's inhabited territory and 89.13% of Serbia's land area. Company has 1.521 active base transceiver stations (BTS). 
The mts mobile network codes are: '''064''' (international: +381 64), '''065''' (international +381 65) and '''066''' (international + 381 66).

===Fixed-line telephony===
Telekom Srbija formerly held a monopoly on all land-line services in Serbia until 2010, when [[Telenor Serbia]] became the second land-line operator in the country.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wirelessweek.com/news/2010/01/telenor-gets-serbias-fixed-phone-license|title=Telenor gets Serbia's fixed phone license|publisher=WirelessWeek|date=22 January 2010|accessdate=2 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407085800/http://www.wirelessweek.com/news/2010/01/telenor-gets-serbias-fixed-phone-license|archive-date=7 April 2014}}</ref> Telekom Srbija has 2.42 million customers. It is the largest operator in Serbia on the fixed telephony market in 2018(the market share is 81.8%).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ratel.rs/uploads/documents/empire_plugin/An%20Overview%20Of%20The%20Telecom%20And%20Postal%20Services%20Market%20In%20The%20Republic%20Of%20Serbia%20In%202018.pdf|title=An Overview Of The Telecom And Postal Services Market In The Republic Of Serbia|publisher=Ratel|date=19 January 2021|access-date=27 January 2021}}</ref>

=== mts Internet===
{{Empty section|date=October 2026}}

=== Digital Television===

Telekom Srbija is the majority owner of sports television channels [[Arena Sport]] and [[Sport Klub]] which broadcast in [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Croatia]], [[Montenegro]], [[North Macedonia]] and [[Serbia]].<ref name="b92">{{cite news|url=http://www.b92.net/biz/vesti/srbija.php?yyyy=2011&mm=08&dd=26&nav_id=537634|title=Telekom: Za Arena Sport 7,7 mil.€|publisher=B92|language=Serbian|date=26 August 2011}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Naslovna|url=https://mtsdoo.com/|access-date=2021-03-21|website=mtsdoo - privatni|language=en-US}}</ref>

Mts offers cable television under the Supernova brand, digital terrestrial pay-TV under the Antena Plus brand, IPTV service under the brand Iris, as well as satellite television under the brand m:sat TV in Serbia and Montenegro.

=== Web portal ===
'''Mondo.rs''' – News portal (political, business, sports, entertainment and interviews from Serbia and around the world).

==Areas served==
===Austria===
Telekom Srbija operates in [[Austria]] as a mobile virtual network operator [[MVNO]] under brand MTEL <ref>[http://www.mtel.at/ MTEL Austria website]</ref>

===Bosnia and Herzegovina===
Telekom Srbija acquired a 65% controlling stake in [[Telekom Srpske]] for 646 million [[euro]]s in 2006, outbidding [[Telekom Austria]] with an offer of 467 million euros. Telekom Srbija also broadcast cable channel [[Arena Sport]] 1,2,3 and 4.{{cn|date=January 2021}}

===Germany===
Telekom Srbija operates in [[Germany]] as a mobile virtual network operator [[MVNO]] under brand MTEL <ref>[http://www.mtelgermany.de/sr/ MTEL Germany]</ref>

===Montenegro===
Telekom Srbija started its operations on Montenegrin market on 16 July 2007, after the company gained license as a third mobile operator as a part of the consortium with Ogalar B.V. company. The consortium offered for the license the sum of €16&nbsp;million. The name for this subsidiary is [[MTEL CG|m:tel]], and is owned 51% by Telekom Srbija. On Montenegrin territory, Telekom Srbija also broadcasts cable channel Arena Sport 1, 2, 3 and 4.{{cn|date=January 2021}}

===North Macedonia===
Telekom Srbija operates in [[North Macedonia]] as a mobile virtual network operator [[MVNO]] under brand MTEL <ref>[http://www.mtel.mk/ MTEL Macedonia]</ref>

===Switzerland===
Telekom Srbija operates in [[Switzerland]] as a mobile virtual network operator [[MVNO]] under brand MTEL <ref>[http://www.mtel.ch/ MTEL Switzerland]</ref>

==Share capital structure==
As of 3 May 2012:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.telekom.rs/telekomeng/Contents/ContentDefault.aspx?temp=0&sid=1291&id=1292|title=Share capital structure|publisher=Telekom Srbija|access-date=17 April 2013|archive-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701195122/http://www.telekom.rs/telekomeng/Contents/ContentDefault.aspx?temp=0&sid=1291&id=1292|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* The [[Serbia|Republic of Serbia]] is the majority owner of the company (58.11%)
* Telekom Srbija a.d. Beograd (20%)
* Citizens of Republic of Serbia (14.95%)
* Employees and former employees of Telekom Srbija a.d. Beograd,(6.94%)

==Subsidiaries==
{{Unreferenced section|date=January 2021}}
Telekom Srbija a.d. Beograd shares in the capital of its related legal entities is as follows:
* [[Mtel (Bosnia and Herzegovina)|"Telekom Srpske"]] a.d. [[Banja Luka]] – 65%
* [[Mtel (Montenegro)|m:tel]] d.o.o. [[Podgorica]] – 51%
* Telus a.d. [[Belgrade|Beograd]] – 100%
* HD-WIN d.o.o. Beograd  – 100%
* GO4YU d.o.o. Beograd – 100%
* mts Antena TV d.o.o. Beograd – 50%
* mts d.o.o. – 100%
* YUNET INTERNATIONAL d.o.o. – 82.026%
* Kopernikus technology d.o.o. Beograd – 100%
* Preduzeće za audio i video komunikacije "AVCOM" d.o.o. Beograd – 100%
* Društvo za inženjering, trgovinu i usluge "Radijus vektor" d.o.o. Beograd – 100%
* Društvo za inženjering, trgovinu i usluge "MASKO" d.o.o. Beograd – 100%
* Preduzeće za promet, usluge, inženjering i telekomunikacije "BPP ING" [[Grocka]] – 100% 
* Telemark systems d.o.o [[Čačak]] – 100%
These legal entities also constitute Telekom Srbija Group together with Telekom Srbija a.d. Beograd as the [[parent company]].
